content:
New figures show public bodies spent a significant £3.4 billion on private consultants last year, an increase of 62% compared to the 2019-20 period. This spending has not returned to pre-pandemic levels, presenting a considerable hurdle for Keir Starmer's government, which intends to cut consultant expenditure by half during its term. KPMG recently secured a government contract valued at up to £223 million for civil servant training. Since Labour came to power, almost £650 million in new consultancy contracts have been issued, with many agreed prior to the change in administration. These include the KPMG deal for civil service education over 15 months, which is the firm's second-largest public sector agreement. An academic expert in finance and accounting, and a Labour peer, described the situation as "scandalous," attributing the issue to an overreliance on consultants who, in his view, offer limited value due to their brief engagement periods with complex organizations.
